chunks: The chiefs among the people who were arrogant asked the weaker ones among them who believed: 'Do you know that Salih has been sent by his Lord?' They said: 'Indeed we believe in what he has been sent with.'

key_terms.اسْتَكْبَرُوا: They were arrogant / held themselves in high esteem
key_terms.اسْتُضْعِفُوا: They were considered weak / the commoners
key_terms.الْمَلَأُ: The chiefs, aristocrats, or elite of a tribe

ai.seo_question: Who were the 'Mala' (chiefs) in the story of Salih and how did they interact with the believers?
ai.summary: In this verse, the aristocratic elite (Al-Mala') challenge the common believers, revealing a socio-political tension where faith is often viewed through the lens of class status. The commoners' resolute affirmation, 'We believe in what he was sent with,' underscores the Shia emphasis on the steadfastness of the humble against the arrogance of the powerful, a theme echoed in the story of the People of the Trench.
